channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Nov 28–4
item.description: The week's sharpest moment is Thursday's special Town Council sitting as an appellate body on a contested HARC approval — a three-story, 34.88-foot addition at 208 S Fir Street that a neighbor has challenged, the kind of hearing that sets precedent for how construction gets reviewed in this town. Before that, Wednesday brings a proposed ordinance to phase out gas-powered lawn equipment townwide, and the TMVOA votes to adopt its 2027 budget and approve a SMART IGA tied to gondola funding. The county commissioners also hold a special session Wednesday to work through 2027 budget adjustments, including wildfire mitigation funding and a Chamber seed-money request.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events - Dec 02 2026 — 2026-12-02
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-12-02
The December 2 CCAASE meeting is largely a calendar and banner housekeeping session for 2026-2027 events, with one item that carries a bit more weight. The commission holds a public hearing on a street closure request from AB Legacy (Telluride Sleighs and Wagons) for the 2027 Telluride Skijoring and Winter Celebration — an expanded footprint compared to the one-year-only approval granted for 2026. The 2027 request adds closure of South Pine St., both sides of Fir St., and extends the closure window from Thursday, March 11 through Monday, March 15. That dates overlap with the Spring Break Festival (March 11–13) is flagged in the staff memo. Beyond skijoring, the board takes up calendar and banner requests from Telluride Arts (Noel Night), Telluride AIDS Benefit (Fashion Week date shift to Feb 18–March 1), and Telluride Youth Lacrosse (May 22–23 tournament), plus a full slate of 2027 single, double, and triple banner hang approvals. The commission also considers adopting its 2027 Special Event Policies — a document that was workshopped in November and returns here for formal action.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearing on expanded street closure for 2027 Skijoring event.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee - Dec 02 2026 — 2026-12-02
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-12-02
The December 2 Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee meeting has one substantive action item: a request from Lela and Jon Martin for an exception to the permitted capital improvement limits under their deed restriction, covering a proposed $160,000 roof replacement at 950 E. Colorado Avenue, Gold Run, Unit 3B. That figure is 57% of their original purchase price of $279,200 — well beyond the 30% absolute cap written into their older deed restriction. Staff recommends approval, conditioned on the Martins executing a new deed restriction under the current Guidelines, which replaced the hard cap with a more flexible exception process. If approved, the unit's maximum sale price would climb significantly, raising affordability-tier questions the subcommittee will need to weigh. The board also takes up minutes from the October 7 and November 18 meetings.
⚡ Why it matters: Housing Authority decides whether to allow $160,000 deed-restricted capital improvement exception.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Ecology Commission - Dec 02 2026 — 2026-12-02
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-12-02
The Ecology Commission takes up a proposed ordinance that would phase out combustion-powered lawn and garden equipment townwide — first for leaf blowers by January 1, 2028, then for all other covered equipment (mowers, trimmers, edgers, and the like) by January 1, 2030. The draft ordinance would also immediately bar the Town from purchasing any new gas-powered lawn equipment. Snow removal gear, chainsaws, portable generators, and wildfire/defensible-space work are carved out. Enforcement would run complaint-based, with a written warning on a first offense; commercial operators can be cited both individually and as a business entity. Colorado's HB23-1161 point-of-sale discount and San Miguel Power Association rebates together could offset roughly half the cost of replacement equipment. This is a work session — no vote is on the table yet — with the path forward likely running through a Town Council agenda item after today's discussion.
⚡ Why it matters: Proposed ordinance would ban gas lawn equipment townwide starting 2028.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of County Commissioner meeting -Special — 2026-12-03
item.description:
San Miguel County • 2026-12-03
A special BOCC session with two distinct parts. First, budget adjustments for 2027: the board will work through potential amendments including clarifying the wildfire mitigation budget, a $50,000 seed-money request from the Chamber of Commerce, and an additional cost contribution tied to a Youth Hangout project. The consent agenda covers routine items — a planning commission reappointment, surplus declaration for three aging Road and Bridge trucks, the annual HUTF mileage sheet, an amended deed restriction in Two Rivers Subdivision, and a Proposition 123 MOU with the City of Montrose. Then, starting around 11:05, the commissioners move into closed executive sessions for personnel reviews of the County Manager and County Attorney, both of whom requested the closed meetings.
⚡ Why it matters: BOCC decides 2027 budget amendments including wildfire mitigation and Chamber funding.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Special Town Council - Dec 04 2026 — 2026-12-04
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-12-04
This special meeting is a single-item public hearing: Town Council sits as an appellate body to review a challenge to HARC's September 16, 2026 approval of a new construction project at 208 S Fir Street. The appellant, an adjacent property owner at 150 W Pacific Avenue, filed the appeal on September 30, 2026. At issue is a three-story, 34.88-foot addition behind a reconstructed historic Supporting structure — bringing the project to 5,033 sq ft on a 3,525 sq ft lot in the Commercial zone, within the Telluride Historic Landmark District. The core argument: HARC approved the building without ever formally determining which design guidelines govern it — whether the replica qualifies as a rated Supporting structure reconstruction (triggering subordination and height standards) or as new construction on a vacant lot. HARC also amended a sequencing condition from its 2021 demolition approval, and the appellant contends that amendment was made without the findings the Land Use Code requires. Council will hear both appeals.
⚡ Why it matters: Council reviews contested HARC approval; outcome sets construction review precedent.
